subject: bicycle
pitch: A vintage Dutch city bicycle in mint green. Tall upright handlebars with cream grips and a silver bell, a brown leather saddle with springs, chrome mudguards, a chain guard, a wicker basket on the front filled with sunflowers and a baguette, and whitewall tyres.
reasoning:
I'm planning a vintage Dutch city bicycle as a single TS module, composing it as an object from primitive shapes like swept tubes, rods, capsules, and lathed or extruded parts for things like fenders and a bell.

I'm working out the real-world geometry: wheel radius around 0.34m, wheelbase roughly 1.07m with rear axle near z=-0.35 and front axle near z=0.72, and placing the bottom bracket, seat tube, and sloping top tube to form a simple diamond frame leading up to the head tube and saddle positions.

Now I'm figuring out the fork legs running from the head tube down to the front axle, then building the handlebar assembly—a tall stem rising to an upright, swept-back bar defined as a curved path of points, meant to mimic the classic Dutch city-bike riser bars.

For the grips, I'm adding tapered cream-colored capsules at the bar ends, with the stem connecting the head tube to the bar's center point. I'm also placing a small silver bell near the right grip using a lathe-generated dome profile for its rounded cap shape, then moving on to position the saddle—a brown leather seat mounted atop the seat post—and start shaping its outline.

Shaping saddle profile...

Now I'm adding the seatpost and a coil spring under the saddle, using a helical sweep to approximate the classic bike spring geometry, positioned near the seat cluster.

For the wheels, I'm building tyres as torus shapes rotated to lie flat against the wheel axis, with a smaller cream-colored torus layered on the sidewall to create the whitewall effect.

Now I'm working out the rims and spokes — a thin silver torus for the rim, and sixteen slender rods per wheel radiating from hub to rim using angular offsets around the circle.

Adding more spoke geometry and the hub cylinder, using a simple rod between two points along the axle as a quicker alternative to a rotated cylinder...

For the rims I'm nesting a thin torus just inside the tyre torus so it reads as the metal wheel edge peeking through. For the fenders, I'm sketching chrome arcs that sweep around the top of each wheel using the arc-sweep helper, rotating about the axle axis to figure out which direction the arc should curve toward the front versus rear of the vehicle.

Working out fender dimensions as a box-section sweep—width along X and radial thickness—sized to clear the wheel with a small gap, mirrored for front and rear. I'm deciding to skip fender struts for simplicity, then moving on to plan a chain guard as a chrome or black half-shell covering the chain.

For the chainring, I'm positioning a flattened cylinder rotated so its axis points along X, placed near the bottom bracket, which I'm setting slightly below the rear axle height for a realistic Dutch bike look. Now I'm thinking through how to extrude an outline that forms a half-disc guard shape covering the chainring from the front-top area.

Defining the chain guard outline...

Then I'm placing the chain as thin black rods connecting the chainring and rear sprocket, aligning them at the same x-offset so the drivetrain sits in one plane, and starting the crank arms as rods extending from the bottom bracket out to the pedal positions.

I'm now laying out the frame tubes—seat tube, seat stays, chain stays, top tube, down tube—and the front fork, choosing coordinates that keep everything roughly aligned into a diamond frame shape while avoiding obvious collisions with the wheels.

I'm settling on a color palette: mint green frame, cream grips, chrome accents, brown leather, black tires, cream whitewalls. For the front basket, I'm planning a frustumBox shape with a woven checkerboard-style paint pattern to mimic wicker, then adding sunflowers made from textured circular cards with a custom SVG texture (petals arranged radially around a brown center) mounted on thin green stems, positioning them so they poke out above the basket without colliding with the handlebars. I'm also working out bracket rods to attach the basket to the handlebar/head area, and sketching a baguette shape lying diagonally in the basket with its ends protruding above the rim.

Now I'm defining the bell, saddle (with spring sweep beneath it), handlebar catmull path with chrome grips, fenders as arc sweeps with box cross-sections, and the chain guard as a half-shell extrusion covering the chainring. I'm working through the chainring and rear sprocket geometry, connecting them with angled chain rods for top and bottom runs, and placing the crank arms and pedal boxes on either side of the bottom bracket. For the wheels, I'm writing a reusable function that builds the tire torus, whitewall ring, chrome rim, hub rod, and a full set of crossed spokes per wheel, keeping part counts reasonable. Finally I'm double-checking the SDK import conventions and part/texture signatures to make sure the flower discs, stems, and all materials render correctly.

I'm adding sunflower details — generating an SVG texture with radiating petals and a dark center disc, then placing several flower heads tilted outward from the basket with stems connecting back to the basket rim, plus a couple of simple extruded leaves for extra visual interest. I'm also laying out the basket itself as a tapered frustum with a wicker-weave paint pattern and a wrapped rim, connected to the handlebars via chrome support rods, while double-checking clearances against the head tube and front wheel. After confirming saddle, bell, and frame colors, I'm moving into writing the actual pedal, crank, grip, and sweep-based fender code, and I'm about to define the arc helper for the fender paths.
